scope: Within-participant recognition of speech versus music conditions in unseen blocks of the same 6.5-minute film. No cross-participant or new-film generalization claim.
block_numbering: One-based order of the 13 speech/music events in each film events.tsv, not BIDS run numbers.

window.eligibility_rule: Keep a candidate only if its full two-second interval and the following two-second guard fit inside the measured block duration. Do not round the duration up, pad, or read across a block boundary.
window.preprocessing: Read only the requested two-second source interval. Resample within each independent window. Do not use a filter, normalization fit, or rereference that uses samples from another split. Fit any learned transformation on train only.

participant_rule: Use one clinical film acquisition per eligible iEEG participant. Do not count a second playback or HDgrid acquisition as a new participant. Reject participants with missing, incomplete, corrupt, or mistimed film data, or no good intracranial channels. Freeze QC rules and the eligible list before evaluator-only Test export.
channel_rule: Use channels marked good with type ECOG or SEEG. Exclude EOG, ECG, EMG, trigger, misc, and bad channels. Keep each participant's montage separate; do not require electrode alignment across participants.
public_inputs: Public train and validation arrays, labels, opaque IDs, anonymous channel types, and processed sampling rate. Shuffle each split. Remove source paths, original onsets, block numbers, run numbers, marker channels, and sequential order.
evaluator_only: Keep Test arrays, Test labels, block membership, original participant mapping, and provenance outside the Agent bundle. A trusted owner can export and score Test after freezing a submission. Public source annotations mean this is an honest-protocol holdout, not a secret blind test.
submission: One finite probability in [0,1] for speech per evaluator-supplied opaque window ID. Missing or extra IDs invalidate the submission.
primary_score: For each participant and each of the four Test blocks, average its window probabilities. Predict speech if the block mean is at least 0.5. Calculate speech recall across two speech blocks and music recall across two music blocks. Their mean is the participant balanced accuracy. Average participant balanced accuracies with equal participant weight.
interpretation_limits: Four Test blocks are four distinct stimulus segments; windows and patients do not create new stimulus segments. The conditions also differ in uncontrolled audiovisual content. Slow neural drift can remain a proxy for movie time even when timestamps are hidden. A temporal nuisance diagnostic is useful before interpreting the score as content-specific neural activity; it is not a task-activation gate. Scores do not isolate a speech mechanism or establish generalization to another film.
